info.bio:
Little Willie John (William Edward John, November 15, 1937 - May 26, 1968), was an American Rhythm & Blues singer who performed in the 1950s and early 1960s. 

Many sources erroneously give his middle name as Edgar. He is best known for his popular music chart successes with songs such as, "All Around the World" (1955), "Need Your Love So Bad" (1956) and "Fever" the same year, the latter covered in 1958 by Peggy Lee. An important figure in early R&B music, Little Willie John was a 1996 Inductee into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

scenes.desc: Fusión de rhythm'n'blues y country, con mucho más peso del primero. Chuck Berry inventa en 1955 el rock'n'roll tal como se conocerá durante cincuenta años (la guitarra como instrumento protagonista, canciones propias que hablan a los adolescentes); Bo Diddley aporta el ritmo «hambone», Little Richard y Esquerita el histerismo y el maquillaje (el primer «decadence-rock»), Jerry Lee Lewis el piano feroz y Sun Records el rockabilly. Elvis Presley es, para Scaruffi, «la primera gran estafa del rock'n'roll». Buddy Holly y Eddie Cochran abren otra vía; en paralelo nacen el soul (Ray Charles), la exótica (Martin Denny, Esquivel), la música electrónica de cinta y, en Gran Bretaña, el skiffle.

podcast.title: Apollo Residency Headliner
podcast.body: Little Willie John, a prominent blues star, headlined James Brown's first residency at the Apollo Theatre. However, Brown and the Famous Flames proved so popular that they were quickly promoted to co-headline status, much to John's annoyance. "But he was still worried about his new group and how they would fare on this residency which also featured Little Richard's old group The Upsetters and was headlined by the blue star Little Willie John."

podcast.title: Remembered by James Brown
podcast.body: Little Willie John was one of the King Records artists whom James Brown remembered and thought about when Brown was producing records for other King artists like Hank Ballard and Bill Doggett in 1969, as part of his effort to pay back dues. "thinking about Little Willie John and other nice things."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Signed by King Records Later
podcast.body: Although Johnny Otis tried to sign him along with The Royals and Jackie Wilson, King Records initially only signed The Royals, but they eventually signed Little Willie John a couple of years later. "King decided they only wanted to sign the royals, though they would sign Little Willie John a couple of years later."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty-Four: "Reet Petite" by Jackie Wilson

podcast.title: Talent Contest Performer
podcast.body: Little Willie John was a blues singer who performed alongside Jackie Wilson and The Royals in talent shows around Detroit, often participating in pre-arranged wins. "They would all perform on the same talent shows and would agree among themselves who was going to win beforehand."
